# Taskbox spec — v2

**Draft — unapproved.** Revised shared understanding confirmed in session Input 4; that authorizes drafting only. Publication explicitly declined in Input 4. Draft revision: v2-r2 (stable due-date sorting). Prior approved inputs: [v1 spec](../../spec.md), [proposal](../../ticket-proposal.md), [milestones](../../milestones.md), [index](../../README.md). See [session](../../../../../feedback-session.md).

## Problem Statement

A single local user can add and list tasks but cannot record calendar deadlines or find tasks due by a date.

## Solution

Extend the offline CLI with optional due dates at creation and inclusive due-by listing. Preserve existing tasks and offline JSON storage.

## User Stories

1. As a local user, I want to add a task title without a due date so existing workflows continue.
2. As a local user, I want `taskbox add TITLE --due YYYY-MM-DD` so a calendar deadline persists with my task.
3. As a local user, I want ordinary `taskbox list` to include all tasks and display supplied due dates, including after a restart.
4. As a local user, I want `taskbox list --due-on-or-before YYYY-MM-DD` to include dated tasks due before or exactly on the supplied date.
5. As a local user, I want undated tasks excluded from cutoff results while remaining available in ordinary listing.
6. As a local user, I want old JSON records without due dates to remain readable and preserved.
7. As a local user, I want malformed/impossible dates rejected with a useful error, nonzero exit, and no store modification.
8. As a local user, I want an empty successful result when nothing matches, filtered results sorted by due date from earliest to latest with ties retaining existing list order, and ordinary listing to retain its current order.

## Implementation Decisions

- Carry forward v1: offline single-user CLI; add titles and list tasks; persist in a user-selected local JSON file; no network, accounts, or sync. Successful commands exit 0; invalid input exits nonzero.
- Commands and flags are as specified in stories 2–4. Due date is optional at creation. Ordinary listing includes dated and undated tasks, with dates displayed when supplied.
- [Glossary](../../../../GLOSSARY.md): a due date is a user-supplied calendar date without time or timezone. Require strict YYYY-MM-DD syntax and a real Gregorian calendar date for both creation and cutoff; accept past dates. Date validation belongs to the command behavior, before any storage mutation.
- Cutoff comparison is inclusive. Missing due dates, including legacy records, do not match cutoff queries. Filtered results sort by due date ascending; equal-date tasks retain their relative order from ordinary listing. Ordinary listing keeps its current order, including after filtered queries. No matches is a successful empty result.
- Existing task titles, completion states, and records remain preserved. No completion behavior changes are introduced.
- Internal representation, classes, module layout, and migration mechanics are left to workers provided these public/storage compatibility contracts hold. No prefactoring requirement is established by this planning-only fixture.

## Testing Decisions

- Agreed seam: public CLI using a temporary user-selected JSON store; no new seam, internal mocks, or schema-shape assertions required.
- Prior art is the approved v1 public-CLI/restart contract; this fixture provides planning history, not executable test infrastructure.
- Named required gate: **taskbox-cli-contract**. Workers must resolve and record its actual executable command before claiming verification. The name alone is not a passing check.
- Cover add without a date; valid dated creation and ordinary display across process restart; legacy records without dates; preservation of existing data; acceptance of past dates; cutoff before/equal/after boundaries; undated exclusion; ascending filtered due-date ordering; stable ties in existing list order; unchanged ordinary-list order before and after queries; empty success; malformed/impossible creation and cutoff dates with useful errors/nonzero exit and unchanged storage.
- Extend existing coverage where available and add missing behavioral cases at the agreed seam. Preserve v1 behavior. No unrelated coverage expansion is required.
- Evidence must include resolved command, exit result, tested source/test identity, logs/output, and temporary-store observations needed to substantiate the contracts. Human milestone QA complements automated verification.

## Role Configuration

| Role | Model | Reasoning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Implementation and repair | GPT-6.1 Sol | Medium |
| Spec reviewer | GPT-6.1 Sol | High |
| Standards reviewer | GPT-6.1 Sol | High |

Use fresh assignments and a 250K active-context target for each role. Reviewers are configured independently. No ticket overrides. Required/default guidance for all roles: [target AGENTS](../../../../AGENTS.md), [glossary](../../../../GLOSSARY.md), this approved-version spec when approved, and ticket-relevant contracts. No additional role guidance was requested. These are planning settings; no runtime assignments are launched here.

## Milestone Contract

See [full proposal](ticket-proposal.md#milestone-contract): preserve accepted M1/ticket 01; M2 contains 02; final M3 contains 03 and cumulatively covers v1 and all v2 work. Human acceptance of M2 gates work in M3. Ticket Done, milestone acceptance, and feature completion are distinct.

## Out of Scope

Date editing, reminders, new completion behavior, times/timezones, network, accounts, sync, software implementation in this exercise, runtime launch, and QA execution.

## Further Notes

Change from v1: optional persisted/displayed due dates, legacy compatibility, inclusive cutoff filtering sorted by ascending due date with stable ties, validation contracts, new tickets 02/03, and M2/M3. Change from initial v2 draft: filtered ordering now sorts by date; ordinary listing retains current order. Ticket 03 coverage and M3 QA change accordingly; membership/dependencies and roles stay as agreed. Initial draft retained in [v2-before-feedback](../v2-before-feedback/spec.md). Ticket 01 and accepted M1 history remain unchanged. No unresolved behavioral decisions remain. Model execution availability and actual check-command resolution are later execution prerequisites, not claims made by this draft.

## Problem Statement

A local reader needs to track books and their read state, exchange lists through CSV without duplicating entries, and find books by title or author without network access.

## Solution

A Python standard-library CLI invoked as `python -m reading_list --store PATH COMMAND`, using one local JSON store (default `./reading-list.json`). Deliver five complete CLI slices in order: add/list, mark-read, export, import, search. No application exists today.

## User Stories

1. As a reader, I want to add a nonblank title and author so I can retain an unread Entry.
2. As a reader, I want stable increasing positive numeric IDs so I can select an Entry reliably across processes.
3. As a reader, I want to list entries in insertion/ID order, including read state, so I can inspect my list.
4. As a reader, I want an absent store to mean an empty list, and first successful mutation to create storage, so setup is minimal.
5. As a reader, I want duplicate additions rejected so my list stays unique.
6. As a reader, I want to mark an Entry read by ID, with repeated marking harmless, so I can track completion.
7. As a reader, I want to export every Entry to quoted UTF-8 CSV so commas, quotes, newlines and Unicode survive interchange.
8. As a reader, I want CSV import to allocate local IDs and preserve read states so lists can move between stores.
9. As a reader, I want import to skip duplicates against storage and earlier rows, keeping the first Entry’s state, so reimport is safe.
10. As a reader, I want malformed CSV rejected before mutation so a bad row cannot partially import a list.
11. As a reader, I want case-insensitive substring search over title or author, including read and unread entries, so I can find books.
12. As a reader, I want actionable failures for invalid input, unknown IDs, corrupt storage and I/O errors so I can correct problems without losing my list.
13. As a reader, I want every feature available offline with one local store so the list remains private and portable.

## Implementation Decisions

- Domain authority: [Entry and Duplicate glossary](../../../../GLOSSARY.md). An Entry is one book title, author and read/unread state. Duplicate equality trims whitespace and casefolds both title and author. No applicable ADR exists.
- Public CLI contract: `add --title TITLE --author AUTHOR`, `list`, `mark-read ID`, `export PATH`, `import PATH`, and `search QUERY`, under the invocation above. These spellings simply render the agreed operations; all required behaviors are below.
- Trim title/author on input; preserve display case; reject empty results. Stable positive increasing IDs are never reassigned. New additions default unread. Duplicate add fails.
- Missing store is empty; successful mutation creates it. List/search never create a missing store. Storage persists across processes. One user/process at a time; concurrency and migrations are excluded.
- `list` and `search` emit a JSON array of objects with `id`, `title`, `author`, `read` (boolean), ordered by insertion/ID. No matches emits `[]`. Add and mark-read print their ID. Export prints entry count; import prints added and skipped counts. Cosmetic whitespace and count wording may be chosen by workers if unambiguous.
- Mark-read unknown ID fails; already-read succeeds without changing state.
- CSV has exactly the ordered header `title,author,read`, UTF-8 encoding, CSV quoting, and literal `true`/`false` states; no IDs. Export includes every Entry in insertion order. Import assigns fresh local IDs, preserving each supplied state. Reject missing/unexpected columns, malformed row widths, invalid states and blank trimmed title/author. A header-only CSV imports zero entries; a file lacking the required header fails.
- Import validates the complete input before writing. Existing entries and earlier accepted rows take precedence on duplicates; skip later matches without changing earlier state. Reimport adds zero. Report added/skipped counts.
- Reject an export/import path equal to the store path (including resolving aliases) before writing. Invalid arguments, unknown IDs, malformed storage, and I/O errors have a nonzero exit and actionable stderr. A failed mutation preserves existing store bytes; never silently replace corrupt storage. Export failures must preserve the store.
- Search trims the query, rejects blank input and matches Unicode-casefolded substrings of title OR author, across both states.
- Persistence internals, schema details beyond observable records, module structure and implementation strategy remain worker decisions. No network dependencies are permitted.

## Testing Decisions

- Agreed public seam: real CLI subprocesses with isolated temporary files; test observable output, exit status and persistent state across process boundaries. No private-function tests or internal mocks. There is no existing application/testing prior art in this fixture.
- Required named gate for every ticket: **CLI regression gate**, `python -m unittest discover -s tests`, run on the ticket’s resulting revision with the cumulative available suite. Standard-library implementation and unittest runner require no third-party dependencies.
- Behavioral coverage follows ticket acceptance criteria: empty/lazy storage, persistence, validation, Duplicate equivalence/state retention, stable IDs, idempotent marking, UTF-8 CSV quoting and round trips, atomic rejection, corrupt storage, actionable I/O failures and search semantics. Representative inputs cover distinct regressions; no coverage percentage target.

# Local reading-list CLI

**Approved plan v1** · Approval: [session input 3](../../../approved-session.md#input-3-verbatim). The human approved the complete displayed v1 bundle, including command spellings, all ticket bodies, milestone definitions, roles and testing. Plan approval only; no QA acceptance, implementation or run launch. No prior version.
Shared understanding was confirmed in session input 2; coherent publication was explicitly approved in session input 3. See the complete [approved proposal](ticket-proposal.md) and [milestones](milestones.md).

## Problem Statement

A local reader needs to track books and their read state, exchange lists through CSV without duplicating entries, and find books by title or author without network access.

## Solution

A Python standard-library CLI invoked as `python -m reading_list --store PATH COMMAND`, using one local JSON store (default `./reading-list.json`). Deliver five complete CLI slices in order: add/list, mark-read, export, import, search. No application exists today.

## User Stories

1. As a reader, I want to add a nonblank title and author so I can retain an unread Entry.
2. As a reader, I want stable increasing positive numeric IDs so I can select an Entry reliably across processes.
3. As a reader, I want to list entries in insertion/ID order, including read state, so I can inspect my list.
4. As a reader, I want an absent store to mean an empty list, and first successful mutation to create storage, so setup is minimal.
5. As a reader, I want duplicate additions rejected so my list stays unique.
6. As a reader, I want to mark an Entry read by ID, with repeated marking harmless, so I can track completion.
7. As a reader, I want to export every Entry to quoted UTF-8 CSV so commas, quotes, newlines and Unicode survive interchange.
8. As a reader, I want CSV import to allocate local IDs and preserve read states so lists can move between stores.
9. As a reader, I want import to skip duplicates against storage and earlier rows, keeping the first Entry’s state, so reimport is safe.
10. As a reader, I want malformed CSV rejected before mutation so a bad row cannot partially import a list.
11. As a reader, I want case-insensitive substring search over title or author, including read and unread entries, so I can find books.
12. As a reader, I want actionable failures for invalid input, unknown IDs, corrupt storage and I/O errors so I can correct problems without losing my list.
13. As a reader, I want every feature available offline with one local store so the list remains private and portable.

## Implementation Decisions

- Domain authority: [Entry and Duplicate glossary](../../GLOSSARY.md). An Entry is one book title, author and read/unread state. Duplicate equality trims whitespace and casefolds both title and author. No applicable ADR exists.
- Public CLI contract: `add --title TITLE --author AUTHOR`, `list`, `mark-read ID`, `export PATH`, `import PATH`, and `search QUERY`, under the invocation above. These spellings simply render the agreed operations; all required behaviors are below.
- Trim title/author on input; preserve display case; reject empty results. Stable positive increasing IDs are never reassigned. New additions default unread. Duplicate add fails.
- Missing store is empty; successful mutation creates it. List/search never create a missing store. Storage persists across processes. One user/process at a time; concurrency and migrations are excluded.
- `list` and `search` emit a JSON array of objects with `id`, `title`, `author`, `read` (boolean), ordered by insertion/ID. No matches emits `[]`. Add and mark-read print their ID. Export prints entry count; import prints added and skipped counts. Cosmetic whitespace and count wording may be chosen by workers if unambiguous.
- Mark-read unknown ID fails; already-read succeeds without changing state.
- CSV has exactly the ordered header `title,author,read`, UTF-8 encoding, CSV quoting, and literal `true`/`false` states; no IDs. Export includes every Entry in insertion order. Import assigns fresh local IDs, preserving each supplied state. Reject missing/unexpected columns, malformed row widths, invalid states and blank trimmed title/author. A header-only CSV imports zero entries; a file lacking the required header fails.
- Import validates the complete input before writing. Existing entries and earlier accepted rows take precedence on duplicates; skip later matches without changing earlier state. Reimport adds zero. Report added/skipped counts.
- Reject an export/import path equal to the store path (including resolving aliases) before writing. Invalid arguments, unknown IDs, malformed storage, and I/O errors have a nonzero exit and actionable stderr. A failed mutation preserves existing store bytes; never silently replace corrupt storage. Export failures must preserve the store.
- Search trims the query, rejects blank input and matches Unicode-casefolded substrings of title OR author, across both states.
- Persistence internals, schema details beyond observable records, module structure and implementation strategy remain worker decisions. No network dependencies are permitted.

## Testing Decisions
